translations.title: Until that the oscuridad creadora of the humanidad...
translations.text:
Until that the oscuridad creadora of the humanidad

Procreadora of pájaro animal and flor

And of all the cosas humillante

Say in silence the last estallido of the light

And the hora quieta

Venga of the mares brincando in his montura


And between I of new in the redonda

Sion of the cuenta of water

And the sinagoga of the espiga

Not diré siquiera shadow of prayer

Or sembraré my simiente of sal

In the more mínimo valle of the cilicio for lamentar


The majestad and the fire of esta death infantil

Not I will kill

His humanidad diciendo truth grave

Ni profanaré the estaciones of the aliento

With another

Elegía a the inocencia and youth.


In it deep with the primer dead yace the hija of Londres,

Of viejos amigos arropada,

The grano already crecido, the negras venas of his mother,

Oculta for the aguas impasibles

Of the jineteante Támesis.

Not existe more that a death primera.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: My héroe desnuda his nervios
translations.text:
My héroe desnuda his nervios a it largo of my cintura

that rige of the cintura until the hombros,

desenvuelve the head that, as a fantasma soñoliento,

is apoya in my mortal regidor,

the espinazo altivo that desprecia the giros and torsiones.

And estos pobres nervios tan atados to the cráneo

duelen over the papel abandonado for his amante

I me abrazo to the love with my garabateo revoltoso

that gime all the hambre of love

and le cuenta a the página his vacío infortunio.

My héroe desnuda my costado and ve a his heart

that marcha as Venus desnuda

for the playa of carne and enrosca his ensangrentado pliegue;

to the despojar my lomos of promesas

promete cierto calor secreto.

Él sostiene the cables of esta caja of nervios

alabando the error mortal

of the nacimiento and of the death, esas dos tristes sotas of ladrones.

and the hambre is emperador; tira él of the cadena, the cisterna is agita.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Diablo encarnado
translations.text:
Diablo encarnado in a serpiente balbuceante,

The planicies centrales of Asia fueron your garden,

In time corpóreo the círculo was despertado,

Tocando the hirsuta manzana in the formas of the pecado,

And God caminando for there, as a guardián with his lira,

Tocaba his perdón desde the colinas of the sky.


Cuándo éramos extraños for the guiados mares,

A media luna artesanal, santa, colgada in the nubes,

The sabios me dicen that aquel garden of the dioses

Conjuraba the bien and the mal in a tree oriental;

That when the luna is alzaba in the brisa virginal

Was black as the bestia and more pálido that the cruz.


In the garden conocimos a nuestro guardián,

In the aguas sagradas that not is congelan in invierno,

It sentimos in the poderosas mañanas of the destierro

Vimos the infierno in a cuerno of sulfuro, the mito eterno,

All the sky in the medianoche of the sol,

And a serpiente with his música in the formas of the time.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A cambio in the climas of the heart
translations.text:
A cambio in the climas of the heart

vuelve seco it húmedo, the bala of oro estalla

over the tumba helada.

A clima in the comarca of the venas

cambia the night in day; the blood between his soles

ilumina to the viviente gusano.


A cambio in the ojo advierte a time

the ceguera until the hueso; and the útero incorpora

a death mientras surge the life.


A shadow in the clima of the ojo

is a medias his light; the sea sondeado irrumpe

over a earth without arpones.

The semilla that of the lomo hace a selva

divide in dos his fruto; and the mitad is escurre

lenta in a viento dormido.


A clima in the carne and the hueso

is seca and húmeda; the viviente and the dead

is mueven as espectros ante the ojo.


A cambio in the clima of the world

vuelve espectro to the espectro; and cada child dentro his mother

is repliega in his doble of shadow.

A cambio echa the luna dentro of the sol,

tira of the ajadas cortinas of the piel;

and the heart entrega a his muertos.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Where a vez the aguas of your rostro
translations.text:
Where a vez the aguas of your rostro

giraron impulsadas for my hélices, sopla your áspero fantasma,

the muertos alzan the mirada;

where a day asomaron the pelo the tritones

a través of your hielo, the viento áspero navega

for the sal, the raíz, the huevas of the peces.


Where a vez your verdes nudos hundieron his atadura

in the cordón of the marea, there camina now

the vegetal destejedor,

with tijeras filosas, empuñando the cuchillo

for cortar the canales in his origen

and derribar the frutos empapados.


Invisibles, your mareas medidoras of the time

irrumpen in the camas galantes of the algas;

the alga of the love is vuelve mustia;

there in torno a your piedras

sombras of children van, that desde his vacío

lloran ante the sea colmado of delfines.


Secos as the tumba, your coloreados párpados

not serán aherrojados mientras the magia is deslice

sabia over the sky and the earth;

habrá corales in your lechos,

habrá serpientes in your mareas,

until that mueran all nuestros juramentos of the sea.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The fuerza that for the verde tallo impulsa the flor
translations.text:
The fuerza that for the verde tallo impulsa the flor

Impulsa my verdes años; the that agosta the raíz of the tree

Is the that me destruye.

I estoy mudo for decirle a the rosa doblada

That dobla my youth the misma invernal fiebre.


The fuerza that impulsa the water between the rocas

Impulsa my roja blood; the that seca the ruidosas corrientes

Vuelve cera the mía.

And estoy mudo for decirles with my boca a my venas

That the misma boca bebe in the corriente of the monte.


The mano that arremolina the water of the estanque remueve the arena;

The that amarra the soplido of the viento

Detiene my vela of sudario.

And estoy mudo for decirle to the verdugo

That his body vil is hecho of my arcilla.


The labios of the time sorben of the manantial;

The love gotea and is recoge, mas the blood vertida

Calmará his pesares.

And estoy mudo for decirle to the viento of a time

That the time ha marcado a sky alrededor of the astros.


And estoy mudo for decirle a the tumba of the amada

That in my sábana avanza encorvado the mismo gusano.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The fuerza that for the verde tallo impulsa a the flor
translations.text:
The fuerza that for the verde tallo impulsa a the flor

impulsa my verdes años; the that marchita the raíz of the tree

is the that me destruye.

And I estoy mudo for decirle a the encorvada rosa

that the misma fiebre invernal dobla my youth.

The fuerza that impulsa the water between the rocas

impulsa my roja blood; the that seca the arroyos parlantes

vuelve cera the míos.

And I estoy mudo for contarle a my venas

cómo the misma boca bebe of the manantial of the montaña.

The mano that arremolina the water of the estanque

remueve the arenas; the that amarra the ráfagas of the viento

iza my vela of sudario.

And I estoy mudo for decirle to the ahorcado

that the barro of the verdugo is hecho of my arcilla.

The labios of the time sorben of the manantial;

the love gotea and is acumula, mas the blood vertida

calmará his pesares.

And I estoy mudo for decirle to the viento in the intemperie

cómo ha trazado the time a sky between the astros.

And I estoy mudo for decirle a the tumba of the amada

that in my sábana avanza encorvado the mismo gusano.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Not entres dócilmente in esa buena night
translations.text:
Not entres dócilmente in esa buena night,

That to the final of the day debería the vejez arder and delirar;

Enfurécete, enfurécete ante the death of the light.


Aunque the sabios entienden to the final that the oscuridad is it correcto,

As a his verbo ningún rayo ha confiado vigor,

Not entran dócilmente in esa buena night.


Llorando the hombres buenos, to the llegar the last ola

For the brillo with that his frágiles obras pudieron haber danzado in a verde bahía,

Is enfurecen, is enfurecen ante the death of the light.


And the locos, that to the sol cogieron to the vuelo in his cantares,

And advierten, demasiado tarde, the ofensa that le hacían,

Not entran dócilmente in esa buena night.


And the hombres graves, that cerca of the death with the vista that is apaga

Ven that esos eyes ciegos pudieron brillar as meteoros and be alegres,

Is enfurecen, is enfurecen ante the death of the light.


And tú, father mio, allá in your cima sad,

Maldíceme or bendíceme with your fieras lágrimas, it ruego.

Not entres dócilmente in esa buena night.

Enfurécete, enfurécete ante the death of the light.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The conversación of the rezos
translations.text:
The conversación of the rezos that van a say

The child that va a dormir and the man in the escaleras

That sube hacia his love moribundo arriba, in his cuarto,

Uno without preocuparse of a quién conmoverá in his sueño

And another anegado in llanto for if ella ha dead,


Is transforman, in the oscuridad, in the eco that know ascenderá

Desde the man in the escaleras and the child junto a his cama.

Desde the earth verde, a the cielos that responden,

The sonidos that producen ambos rezos

(For a sueño in earth segura and for the love that muere)

Is elevarán with igual congoja. ¿A quién aliviarán?

¿Dormirá the child a salvo or the man llorará?

The conversación of the rezos that serán dichos

Trata over vivos and muertos, and the man in the escaleras

Esta night not hallará agonizando sino vivo and caliente

For the fire of his cuidado a his love in the cuarto of arriba.


And the child, descuidado of hacia quién eleva his rezo,

Is hundirá in a pena tan honda as his propia tumba,

And notará that the ola of eyes negros, a través of the eyes of the sueño,

Le arrastra escaleras arriba hacia alguien that ha dead.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: And the death not tendrá señorío
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: And the death perderá his dominio
translations.text:
And the death perderá his dominio.

The muertos desnudos serán a alone dead.

With the man in the viento and the Luna of occidente;

when is descarnen the huesos and desaparezcan the huesos.

Where hubo codos and pies aparecerán estrellas.

And aunque is sumerjan in profundas aguas tendrán that resurgir.

And aunque the amantes is extravíen perdurará the love.

And the death perderá his dominio.


And the death perderá his dominio.

Bajo the remolinos of the sea

aquellos that yazgan largamente not morirán in the tempestad

retorciéndose in the tormento, when cedan the tendones

atados a a rueda not podrán destrozarse;

between his manos the fe is romperá in dos

and the Unicornio of the mal the atravesará.

And hendidos for all partes not is desmembrarán.

And the death perderá his dominio.


And the death perderá his dominio.

Nunca more the gaviotas gritarán in his oídos

or is romperán the olas tumultuosamente in the ribera;

there where is abrió a flor nunca more another flor

ofrecerá his head a the golpes of the lluvia.

And aún locas or muertas as clavos

atravesarán the margaritas with his cabezas of señoras;

irrumpiendo over the Sol until that the Sol is desprenda.

And the death perderá his dominio.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Of the suspiros algo nace
translations.text:
Of the suspiros algo nace

that not is the pena, because the he abatido

antes of the agonía; the espíritu crece

olvida and weeps:

algo nace, is prueba and sabe bueno,

all not podía be desilusión:

tiene that haber, God sea loado, a certeza,

if not of bien amar, to the menos of not amar,

and esto is verdadero luego of the derrota permanente.


Después of esa lucha that the more débiles conocen.

there is algo more that death;

olvida the grandes sufrimientos or seca the heridas,

él sufrirá for mucho time

because not is arrepiente of abandonar a woman that espera

for his soldado sucio with saliva of words

that derraman a blood tan ácida.


If eso bastase, bastaría for calmar the sufrimiento,

arrepentirse when is ha consumido

the gozo that in the sol me hizo feliz,

qué feliz fui mientras duró the gozar,

if bastara the vaguedad and the mentiras dulces fueran suficiente,

the frases huecas podrían soportar all the sufrimiento

and curarme of males.


If eso bastase: hueso, blood and nervio,

the mente retorcida, the lomo claramente formado,

that busca a tientas the sustancia bajo the plato of the perro,

the man debería curarse of his mal.

Pues all it that existe for give I it ofrezco:

unas migas, a granero and a cabestro.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The jorobado in the parque
translations.text:
The jorobado in the parque

solitario señor

apuntalado between the árboles and the water

desde that the candado of the garden is abre

for that entren the árboles and the water

until the lóbrega campana dominguera in the crepúsculo,


come the pan that ha traído in a diario

bebe the water of the jarro encadenado

that the children llenaron of pedruscos

in the estanque where hice navegar my barco,

for the night durmió in a perrera

but without that nadie le pusiera cadenas.


As the pájaros of the parque ha venido temprano

is sentó as the water

and señor it llamaban eh señor

the chiquillos bribones of the lugar

that escapaban apenas the oía

until alejarse of his vista


more allá of the lago and the rosales

riéndose when the another agitaba his diario

encorvado in the burla

pasaban for the zoológico sonoro of the arboleda of the sauces

esquivando to the cuidador of the parque

with his palo of juntar the hojas.


And the old perro aletargado

solitario between the niñeras and the cisnes

mientras desde the sauces the chiquillos

hacían that the tigres saltaran of his eyes

for rugir between the piedras rocosas

and the bosques is azulaban of marineros


trabajó the day entero until the hora of cerrar

in a figura of woman without fallas

erguida as a young olmo

alta and erguida surgió of his huesos torcidos

for that of night is pusiese of pie

tras the cerrojos and the cadenas


All the night in the parque deshecho

tras the arbustos and the rejas

the pájaros the pasto the árboles the lago

and the children inocentes as fresas

habían ido in pos of the jorobado

until his perrera in the sombras.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Insomnio
translations.text:
Madrid is a ciudad of more of a millón of cadáveres (según the últimas estadísticas).

A veces in the night I me revuelvo and me incorporo in este nicho in the that hace 45 años that me pudro,

and paso largas horas oyendo gemir to the huracán, or ladrar the perros, or fluir blandamente the light of the luna.

And paso largas horas gimiendo as the huracán, ladrando as a perro enfurecido, fluyendo as the leche of the ubre caliente of a gran vaca amarilla.

And paso largas horas preguntándole a God, preguntándole for qué is pudre lentamente my alma,

for qué is pudren more of a millón of cadáveres in esta ciudad of Madrid,

for qué mil millones of cadáveres is pudren lentamente in the world.

Dime, ¿qué huerto quieres abonar with nuestra podredumbre?

¿Temes that is you sequen the grandes rosales of the day, the tristes azucenas letales of your noches?
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Sueño of the dos ciervas
translations.text:
1


¡Oh terso claroscuro of the durmiente!

Derribadas the lindes, fluyó the sueño.

Only the espacio.


Light and shadow, dos ciervas velocísimas,

huyen hacia the fontana of aguas frescas,

centro of all.


¿Vivir not is more that the roce of his viento?

Fuga of the viento, angustia, light and shadow:

forma of all.


And the ciervas, the ciervas incansables,

flechas emparejadas hacia the hito,

huyen and huyen.


The tree of the espacio. (Duerme the man)

To the fin of cada rama there is a estrella.

Night: the siglos.


2


…The tree of the espacio. Duerme the man.

To the fin of cada rama there is a estrella.

Night: the siglos.


Duerme and is agita with terror: comprende.

Ha comprendido, and is le eriza the alma.

¡Gélido sueño!


Huye the gran tree that florece estrellas,

huyen the ciervas of the pies veloces,

huye the fuente.


¿For qué nos huyes, God, for qué nos huyes?

Your veste in rastro, your cabello in cauda,

¿dónde is anegan?


¿There is a hondón, bocana of the espacio,

negra rotura hacia the nada, where

viertes your aliento?


Ay, nunca formas llegarán a esencia,

nunca ciervas a fuente fugitiva.

¡Ay, nunca, nunca!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A the that van a be born
translations.text:
¡Cuán cerca todavía

of the manos of God! ¿Sentís his aliento

rugir between the cedros of the Levante?

¿There is in vuestras pupilas rabos of oro,

vedijitas, aún, incandescentes,

of the gran lumbrarada creadora?

¿Or fraguasteis, tal vez, in his sonrisa

-sonrisillas of God, children dormidos-

and juerga in vuestras salas,

child eternal, gran inventor of juegos?

Oh, vosotros le veis, seres profundos,

and saltáis in the vientre of the mother.


¿Qué peces of colores

os surcan aguas of the dorado sueño?

¿Qué divinos esquifes

-juguetes without engaño-

cruzan the day albar of vuestro cauce?

¿Of qué extraña ladera

son esas pedrezuelas diminutas

that bullen to the manar of vuestras aguas?

Oh fuentes silenciosas.

Oh soterradas fuentes

of the enormes ríos of the life.


Seréis torrente in furia

that va a rodar to the páramo. Seréis

indagación and grito without respuesta.

Ay, guardad esta light estremecida.

Ay, refrenad the water,

volved to the centro exacto.

Ay of vosotros.


… Ay of estos cieguecitos

of leche not cuajada,

of tierna pulpa vegetal, dormida.

Ay, copos of manteca,

that hacia the mercado vais –of his ordeños

modelados for God, aún in his música,

with the gotas aún of his rocío-

between the verdes hojas of the úteros.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Monstruos
translations.text:
All the días rezo esta prayer

to the levantarme:


Oh God,

not me atormentes more.

Dime qué significan

estos espantos that me rodean.

Cercado estoy of monstruos

that mudamente me preguntan,

igual, igual, that I les interrogo a ellos.

That tal vez you preguntan,

it mismo that I in vano perturbo

the silence of your invariable night

with my desgarradora interrogación.

Bajo the penumbra of the estrellas

and bajo the terrible tiniebla of the light solar,

me acechan eyes enemigos,

formas grotescas that me vigilan,

colores hirientes lazos me están tendiendo:

¡son monstruos,

estoy cercado of monstruos!


Not me devoran.

Devoran my reposo anhelado,

me hacen be a angustia that is desarrolla a sí misma,

me hacen man,

monstruo between monstruos.


Not, ninguno tan horrible

as este Dámaso frenético,

as este amarillo ciempiés that hacia ti clama with all his tentáculos enloquecidos,

as esta bestia inmediata

transfundida in a angustia fluyente;

not, ninguno tan monstruoso

as esa alimaña that brama hacia ti,

as esa desgarrada incógnita

that now you increpa with gemidos articulados,

that now you dice:

«Oh God,

not me atormentes more,

dime qué significan

estos monstruos that me rodean

and este espanto íntimo that hacia ti gime in the night.»
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Of profundis
translations.text:
If vais for the carretera of the arrabal, apartaos, not os inficione my pestilencia.

The dedo of my God me ha señalado: odre of putrefacción quiso that fuera este my body,

and a ramera of solicitaciones my alma,

not a ramera fastuosa of the that hacen languidecer of love to the príncipe

over the cabezo of the valle, in the palacete of verano,

sino a loba of the arrabal, acoceada for the trajinantes,

that already ha olvidado the words of love,

and only puede pedir unas monedas of cobre in the cantonada.


I I am the piltrafa that the tablajero arroja to the perro of the mendigo,

and the perro of the mendigo arroja to the muladar.

But desde the mina of the maldades, desde the pozo of the miseria,

my heart is ha levantado until my God,

and le ha dicho: Oh Señor, tú that has hecho also the podredumbre,

mírame,

I I am the orujo exprimido in the año of the mala cosecha,

I I am the excremento of the can sarnoso,

the zapato without suela in the carnero of the camposanto,

I I am the montoncito of estiércol a medio make, that nadie compra

and where casi ni escarban the gallinas.


But you amo,

but you amo frenéticamente.

¡Déjame, déjame fermentar in your love,

deja that me pudra until the entraña,

that is me aniquilen until the últimas briznas of my be,

for that a day sea mantillo of your huertos!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Imitación
translations.text:
A ola insondable of invencible orgullo,
a misterio and a sueño, tal debió parecer my
primera edad. I añado that ese sueño estaba
atravesado for a pensamiento huraño, siempre
despierto, of seres that han existido, and that my
espíritu not hubiera apercibido jamás if the
hubiera dejado pasar cerca of my, bajo my ensoñadora
pupila. That ningún another, acá abajo,
herede esta visión of my espíritu, of esos pensamientos
that a cada instante quisiera dominar
and that is extienden as a hechizo over my
alma. Because, to the fin, esa brillante esperanza
and ese time liviano is han ido, and my reposo
terrestre, me ha dejado, él also, with a
suspiro, to the pasar. Between tanto, not me preocupo
of that él perezca with a pensamiento that
then amaba….!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Alone
translations.text:
Desde the time of my niñez, not he sido
as other were, not he visto
as other veían, not pude sacar
my pasiones desde a común primavera.
Of the misma fuente not he tomado
my pena; not is despertaría
my heart a the joy with the mismo tono;
and all it that quise, it quise alone.
Then -in my niñez- in the amanecer
of a very tempestuosa life, is sacó
desde cada depth of it bueno and it malo
the misterio that todavía me ata:
desde the torrente or the fuente,
desde the rojo peñasco of the montaña,
desde the sol that alrededor of mí giraba
in his otoño teñido of oro,
desde the rayo in the sky
that pasaba junto a mí volando,
desde the trueno and the tormenta,
and the nube that tomó the forma
(when the resto of the sky was azul)
of a demonio ante my vista.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The estrella of the tarde
translations.text:
Was in the heart of the verano and in medio of
the night. The estrellas marchando in his órbitas
brillaban with a pálido resplandor a través
of the light more viva of the fría luna, mientras that
ésta, rodeada of the planetas, his esclavos,
lanzaba desde it alto of the cielos, his rayos
over the olas.


                            ——


I contemplaba his sad sonrisa, demasiado
fría, demasiado fría for mí. A nube oscura
vino a pasar, semejante a a sudario, and fué
then that me volví hacia ti, Estrella of the
Sur, orgullosa in your gloria lejana. And now
me será more querida your light, because it that me
traes of more magnificente a través of the sky
nocturno, is the joy of my heart, and I prefiero
your discreto and lejano resplandor a esa llama
cercana but more fría!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Soneto a the ciencia
translations.text:
¡Ciencia! ¡verdadera hija of the time tú you are!
            that alteras all the cosas with your escrutadores eyes.
            ¿For qué devoras así the heart of the poeta,
            buitre, cuyas alas son obtusas realidades?


            ¿Cómo debería él amarte? or ¿cómo puede juzgarte sabia
            aquel a quien not dejas in his vagar
            buscar a tesoro in the enjoyados cielos,
            aunque is elevara with intrépida ala?


            ¿Not has arrebatado a Diana of his carro?
            ¿Ni expulsado a the Hamadríades of the bosque
            for buscar abrigo in alguna feliz estrella?


            ¿Not has arrancado a the Náyades of the inundación,
            to the Elfo of the verde hierba, and a mí
            of the sueño of verano bajo the tamarindo?
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A ensueño in a ensueño
translations.text:
Recibid este beso in the frente. And now that
os dejo, permitidme for it menos confesar esto:
not os agraviéis, vos that estimáis that my días
han sido a ensueño. Entretanto, if the esperanza
is ha ido, in a night or in a day,
in a visión or in a sueño, ¿is ha ido menos
for eso? All it that we see or nos parece, not
is sino a ensueño in a ensueño!


                             ——


Me encuentro in medio of the bramidos of
a costa atormentada for the resaca, and tengo
in the mano granos of arena of oro. ¡Cuán
poco is! ¡And cómo is deslizan a través of my
dedos hacia the abismo, mientras lloro, mientras
lloro! ¡God mío, ¿not puedo retenerlos in a
nudo more seguro? ¡God mío!, ¿not podré
salvar uno alone of the cruel vacío? ¿All it that
we see or nos parece not is another cosa that a
ensueño in a ensueño?
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Lucero vespertino
translations.text:
Ocurrió a medianoche
            a mediados of verano;
            lucían pálidas estrellas
            tras the potente halo
            of a luna clara and fría
            that iluminaba the olas
            rodeada of planetas,
            esclavos of his señora.
            Detuve my mirada
            in his sonrisa helada
            -demasiado helada for mí-;
            a nube le puso a velo
            of lanudo terciopelo
            and then me fijé in ti.
            Lucero orgulloso,
            remoto, glorioso,
            I siempre your brillo preferí;
            pues my alma jalea
            the orgullosa tarea
            that cumples of the night a the mañana,
            and admiro more, desde luego,
            your lejanísimo fire
            that esa another light, more fría, more cercana.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Balada nupcial
translations.text:
In my dedo the anillo,

the guirnalda nupcial my sien decora;

of sedas and diamantes busco the brillo,

and I am feliz now.


And my señor me brinda love seguro;

but to the decirme ayer cuánto me adora,

tembló my heart, as to the conjuro,

of “quien cayó in the guerra”, to the pie of the muro,

and that is feliz now.


But él tranquilizome, and in my frente

besó the palidez that it enamora.

And he here that in a ensueño, vi presente,

to the dead D’Elormy: -suyo, in my frente,

was the beso; and suspiré (¡cuán dulcemente!):

“-¡Ah, I am feliz now!”


And if pude otorgar word nueva,

así the voto juré, and aunque traidora,

and aunque a luto of love the alma lleva,

vean brillar ese anillo that “me prueba”

that I am feliz now.


¡Ah! ilumíneme God aquel pasado,

pues if sueña or not sueña the alma ignora,

and the heart is oprime, and conturbado

pregúntase, oh Señor, if the “Olvidado”

será feliz now!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Espíritus of the Night
translations.text:
Your alma, in the tumba of piedra gris
estará a solas with his tristes pensamientos.


Ningún be humano you espiará
a the hora of your secreto.


¡Permanece callado in esa soledad!


Not estás completamente abandonado:
the espíritus of the death, in the life, you buscan
and, in the death, you rodean.


You cubrirán of sombras: ¡Permanece callado!
The night, tan clara, is oscurecerá
and the estrellas not mirarán the earth,
desde his altísimos tronos in the sky,
with his light of esperanza for the mortales.


But his globos rojos apagados,
in your hastío, tendrán the forma
of a incendio and of a fiebre
that you poseerán for siempre.


Of your espíritu not podrás desechar the visiones,
that now not serán rocío over the hierba.


The brisa – the aliento of God – is silenciosa,
and the niebla over the colina,
oscura, very oscura, but inmaculada,
is a símbolo and a señal.


¡As is extiende over the árboles
the misterio of the misterios.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Of all cuantos anhelan your presencia
translations.text:
Of all cuantos anhelan your presencia
as a mañana,
Of all cuantos padecen your ausencia
as a night,
As the destierro inapelable of the sol sacred
Allende the firmamento; of all the dolientes that a cada instante
You bendicen for the esperanza, for the life, ah,
and over all,
For haberles devuelto the fe extraviada, enterrada
In the truth, in the virtud, in the raza of the man…


Of all aquellos that, when agonizaban
in the lecho impío
Of the desesperanza, is han incorporado of pronto
To the oírte susurrar with dulzura: “¡That haya light!”,
To the oírte susurrar esas words acentuadas
For the sereno brillo of your eyes…


Of all your numerosos deudores,
cuya gratitud
Raya the veneración, recuerda, oh,
not olvides nunca
A your devoto more ferviente, to the more incondicional,
And piensa that estas líneas vacilantes
the habrá escrito él,
Ese that now, to the escribirlas,
is emociona pensando
That his espíritu comulga with the espíritu
of a ángel.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Eulalia
translations.text:
Vivía only in a world of lamentaciones and
my alma was a onda estancada, until that
the bella and dulce Eulalia llegó a be my pudorosa
compañera, until that the young Eulalia, the of
the cabellos of oro, llegó a be my sonriente
compañera.


                               ——


¡Ah! the estrellas of the night brillan bastante
menos that the eyes of esa radiante niña!
And jamás girón of vapor emergido in a irisado
claro of luna, podrá compararse to the bucle more
descuidado of the modesta Eulalia, podrá
compararse to the bucle more humilde and more descuidado
of Eulalia, the of the brillantes eyes!


                              ——


The duda and the pena not me invaden jamás,
now, because his alma me entrega suspiro for
suspiro. And durante all the day, Astarté resplandece
brillante and fuerte in the sky, in tanto that
siempre hacia ella, my querida Eulalia, levanta
his eyes of esposa, in tanto that siempre hacia
ella my young Eulalia eleva his bellos eyes
violetas!…
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The valle of the inquietud
translations.text:
Hubo here a valle antaño, callado and sonriente,
where nadie habitaba:
partiéronse the gentes a the guerra,
dejando a the luceros, of eyes dulces,
that velaran, of night, desde azuladas torres,
the flores, and in the centro of the valle, cada day,
the roja light of the sol is posaba, indolente.
Mas already quien it visite advertiría
the inquietud of ese valle melancólico.
Not there is in él nada quieto,
sino the aire, that ampara
aquella soledad of maravilla.
¡Ah! Ningún viento mece aquellos árboles,
that palpitan to the modo of the helados mares
in torno of the Hébridas brumosas.
¡Ah! Ningún viento arrastra aquellas nubes,
that crujen levemente for the sky intranquilo,
turbadas desde the alba until the night,
over the violetas that there yacen,
as eyes humanos of mil suertes,
over ondulantes lirios,
that lloran in the tumbas ignoradas.
Ondulan, and of his fragantes cimas
cae eterno rocío, gota a gota.
Lloran, and for his tallos delicados,
as aljófar, van lágrimas perennes.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The lago
translations.text:
In the primavera of my youth, was my destino

not frecuentar of all the vasto world sino

a alone lugar that amaba more that all the other,

tanta was of amable the soledad of his lago salvaje,

rodeado for negros peñascos and of altos

pinos that dominaban his alrededores.


——


But when the night tendía his sudario over

ese lugar as over all the cosas, and is agregaba

the místico viento murmurando his melodía,

then, ¡oh, then is despertaba

siempre in mí the terror for ese lago solitario!


——


And without embargo ese terror not was miedo, sino

a turbación deliciosa, a sentimiento that

ninguna mina of piedras preciosas podría inspirarme

or convidarme a definir, ni the love

mismo, aunque ese love fuera the tuyo.


——


The death reinaba in the seno of esa onda

envenenada, and in his remolino había a tumba

bien hecha for aquel that pudiera beber in

ella a consuelo a his imaginación taciturna, for

aquel cuya alma desamparada pudiera haberse

hecho a Edén of ese lago velado.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The valle intranquilo
translations.text:
Hubo a time in that the valle sonreía,

silencioso, aunque nadie there vivía;

his gente había marchado hacia the guerra

confiando the cuidado of esa sierra,

for the night, a the mirada fiel

of the estrellas desde his azul cuartel

and of day, a the rojos resplandores

of the sol that dormitaba between the flores.

Mas now for all visitante

the valle sad is inquieto e inquietante.

Nada there is detiene a alone instante…

nada salvo the aire that is cierne

over the soledad mágica and perenne.

¡Ah, ningún viento agita the ramajes

that palpitan as the glacial oleaje

in torno a the Hébridas salvajes!

¡Ah, ningún viento empuja the furtivo

manto of nubes that, without respiro,

surcan durante the day the sky esquivo

over the violetas there esparcidas

as eyes humanos of mil medidas…!

over the ondeantes azucenas

that lloran junto a the tumbas ajenas!

Ondean: and in his pétalos more tiernos

is juntan gotas of rocío sempiterno.

Lloran: and for his tallos claudicantes

bajan perennes lágrimas as diamantes.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The day more feliz, the hora more dichosa, the ha...
translations.text:
The day more feliz, the hora more dichosa, the ha

conocido my heart agotado and marchito; but

siento that ha desaparecido already my more alta esperanza

of orgullo and of poderío.


——


¿He dicho of poderío? Sí. But desde hace

largo time, ¡ay of mí! is han desvanecido

the bellos ensueños of the youth; han pasado

already: dejémoslos that is desvanezcan!


——


And tú, orgullo, ¿qué haré of ti now? Another

frente puede bien heredar the veneno that me

has dado. That for it menos my espíritu permanezca

tranquilo.


——


The day more hermoso, the hora more feliz that my

eyes hayan visto and hayan podido see jamás,

my more brillante mirada of orgullo and of poderío,

all eso ha existido but already not existe; I

it siento.


——


And if esa esperanza of orgullo and of poderío

me fuera ofrecida now acompañada of a

pain semejante to the that experimento, not quisiera

revivir esa hora brillante.


——


Because bajo his ala llevaba a oscura

mezcla and mientras volaba, dejaba caer a

esencia todopoderosa for consumir a alma that

tan bien the conocía.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Peán
translations.text:
I


¿Cómo será leído the rito of the entierro?

¿The solemne canción cantada?

¿The réquiem for the more bella dead,

that haya dead tan young?


II


His amigos están contemplándola,

in his vistoso féretro.

¡And lloran! ¡Oh!, deshonrar

the belleza dead, with a lágrima!


III


Ellos the amaban for his riqueza

the odiaban for his orgullo.

But ella creció with salud feble,

and ellos the aman, pues murió.


IV


Ellos me dicen (mientras hablan

of his “costosa mortaja bordada”)

that my voice is is volviendo débil,

that not debería cantar of ningún modo.


V


¡Oh, that my tono debiera

adecuarse a tan solemne canción

tan lastimera, tan lastimera,

that the dead not sintiese agravio.


VI


But ella is ha ido arriba,

with the young esperanza a his lado,

and I estoy embriagado with the love

of the dead, that is my novia.


VII


Of the dead of the dead that yace

all perfumada here,

with the death in the eyes,

and the life in the cabello.


VIII


Así in the ataúd recio and largo

I golpeo. The susurro enviado

for the grises cámaras a my canción

será the acompañamiento.


IX


Tú bien moriste in the junio of your life,

but not moriste demasiado bella

not moriste demasiado pronto,

not with demasiada calma in the aire.


X


For eso, for ti esta night

not elevaré a réquiem,

but you llevaré in your vuelo,

with a peán of antaño.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Ojalá my young life fuera a sueño duradero
translations.text:
¡Ojalá my young life fuera a sueño duradero!
And my espíritu durmiera until that the rayo certero
Of a eternidad anunciara the new day.
¡Sí! Aunque the largo sueño fuera of agonía
Siempre sería mejor that be despierto
For quien tuvo, desde the nacimiento
In the dulce earth, the heart
Prisionero of the caos of the pasión.


Mas if ese sueño persistiera eternamente
As the sueños infantiles in my mente
Solían persistir, if eso ocurriera,
Sería ridículo esperar a quimera.
Because he soñado that the sol resplandecía
In the sky estival, lleno of light bravía
And of belleza, and my heart he paseado
For climas remotos e inventados,
Junto a seres imaginarios, only previstos
For mí… ¿qué more podría haber visto?.


But a vez, a única vez, and already not olvidaré
Aquel bárbaro momento, a poder or not is qué
Hechizo me ciñó, or was that the viento helado
Sopló of night and to the marchar dejó grabado
In my espíritu his rastro, or was the Luna
That brilló in my sueños with especial fortuna
And frialdad, or the estrellas… in cualquier caso
The sueño was as ese viento: démosle paso.


I he sido feliz, pues, aunque the sistema
Fuera a sueño. Fui feliz, and adoro the tema:
¡Sueños!. Tanto for his intenso colorido
That oponen a it real, and because to the ojo delirante
Ofrecen cosas more bellas and abundantes
Of the paraíso and of the love, ¡and all nuestras!
That the esperanza young in his mejores muestras.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Imaginación
translations.text:
The pura imaginación deriva tanto of the belleza as of fealdad, únicamente the cosas mas combinables and that not han sido combinadas until the momento; for regla general, the compuesto resultante participa of the belleza or of the sublimidad in razón of the respectiva belleza or sublimidad of the cosas combinadas, that todavía is consideran as atómicas, is say, as combinaciones previas.


But it that with frecuencia sucede análogamente in the química física is da with the misma facilidad in the química inteligente, and as¡ mezcla of dos elementos da as resultado algo that not posee the cualidades of ellos, or incluso nada of the cualidades of ambos.


Así, the gama of the imaginación resulta ilimitada. His materiales is extienden for all the universo. Incluso of the deformidad consigue esa belleza that is to the mismo time his único objeto and his inevitable prueba.


But, in general, the riqueza, the fuerza of the materiales combinados, the facilidad of describir novedades that valgan the pena combinarse, and in especial “the absoluta combinación química” of the masa absoluta, son the detalles that debemos considerar in nuestra estima of the imaginación.


The completa armonía of a obra imaginativa with frecuencia is the causa of that the irreflexivos the supervaloren, dado the carácter obvio that is sobreañade a ella. We are very dueños of preguntarnos for that semejantes combinaciones not habían sido imaginadas antes.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The espíritus of the muertos
translations.text:
Your alma is encontrará sola, cautiva of the
negros pensamientos of the gris piedra tumbal;
ninguna persona you inquietará in your horas of
recogimiento.


                            ——


Quédate silenciosamente in esa soledad that
not is abandono,—because the espíritus of the
muertos that existieron antes that tú in the life,
you alcanzarán and you rodearán in the death,—and
the shadow proyectada over your cara obedecerá
a his voluntad; for it tanto, permanece tranquilo.


                            ——


Aunque serena, the night fruncirá his ceño,
and the estrellas, of it alto of his tronos celestes,
not bajarán more his miradas with a resplandor
parecido to the of the esperanza that is concede a
the mortales; but his órbitas rojas, desprovistas
of all rayo, serán for your heart marchito
as a quemadura, as a fiebre
that querrá unirse a ti for siempre.


                            ——


Now, you visitan pensamientos that not ahuyentarás
jamás; now surgen ante ti visiones
that not is desvanecerán jamás; jamás ellas dejarán
your espíritu, but is fijarán as gotas
of rocío over the hierba.


                            ——


The brisa,—esa respiración of God,—reposa
inmóvil, and the bruma that is extiende as a
shadow over the colina,—as a shadow cuyo
velo not is ha desgarrado todavía,—resulta así
a símbolo and a signo. As logra permanecer
suspendida a the árboles, ese is the misterio
of the misterios!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Israfel
translations.text:
In the Sky mora a espíritu,
cuyas cuerdas of the heart son a laúd;
ninguno canta mejor, ni with tal frenesí
as the ángel Israfel,
and the estrellas vertiginosas,
así it afirma the leyenda,
deteniendo his himnos,
escuchan the encantamiento of his voice,
all in silence.
Dudando in it alto of his meridiano,
the luna apasionada is sonroja of love,
mientras, for oírle, the mismo rayo
(and with él the veloces Pléyades)
is detienen in the sky.
And dicen that the fervor of Israfel
is debe to the sortilegio of his lira,
to the trémulo alambre vivo of his cuerdas;
where the pensamientos profundos son a deber,
where the Love is a God already anciano,
where the eyes of the huríes
brillan with the adorada belleza of the astros.
Tienes razón, Israfel,
in despreciar all canto that not sea apasionado.
¡A ti the laureles, bardo the mejor
and the more sabio!
¡Larga and gozosa life for ti!
The altos éxtasis caen with the ardientes notas,
with your pain, your joy, your odio, your love,
the fervor of your laúd.
¿Qué there is of extraño in that the estrellas
eternas permanezcan mudas?
Sí, tuyo is the Sky,
but este is a world of dulce amargura,
nuestras flores son only flores,
and the shadow of your inmensa beatitud
is the light of nuestro sol.
If I pudiese habitar in the reino of Israfel,
and él in where I habito,
not podría the ángel cantar a melodía terrenal,
mientras I, in cambio, podría lanzar to the firmamento
a nota more plena that esta sad canción
that brota of my lira.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Annabel Lee
translations.text:
Hace muchos, muchos años

in a reino junto to the sea

vivió a doncella that tal vez conozcas

llamada Annabel Lee.

And esta doncella vivía without another pensamiento

that amarme and be amada for mí.


Ambos éramos children

in este reino junto to the sea

but amábamos with a love that was more that love

I and my Annabel Lee

with love that the alados serafines of the sky

nos envidiaban a ella and a mí.


And for esta razón, hace mucho time,

in este reino junto to the sea

of a nube sopló a viento

that heló a my amada Annabel Lee.

And his parientes of alta cuna vinieron

and is the llevaron lejos of mí

for encerrarla in a sepulcro

in este reino junto to the sea.


The ángeles, descontentos in the sky,

nos envidiaron a ella and a mí.

¡Sí! For esta razón (as all know

in este reino junto to the sea)

the viento salió of the nube for the night

for helar and matar a my Annabel Lee.


But nuestro love was mucho more fuerte

that the of aquellos mayores

or more sabios that nosotros.

And ni the ángeles arriba in the sky

ni the demonios debajo of the sea

jamás podrán separar my alma of the alma

of the hermosa Annabel Lee.


Pues the luna nunca resplandece without traerme sueños

of the hermosa Annabel Lee

and the estrellas nunca brillan without that I sienta the eyes radiantes

of the hermosa Annabel Lee

and when llega the marea nocturna, me acuesto justo to the lado

of my amada -my amada- my life and my prometida

in his sepulcro there junto to the sea

in his tumba junto to the ruidoso sea.




Traducción of Luis López Nieves
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The reino of the hadas
translations.text:
Valles oscuros, torrentes umbríos, bosques
nebulosos in the cuales nadie puede descubrir
the formas a causa of the lágrimas that gota a
gota is lloran of all partes! Allá, lunas desmesuradas
crecen and decrecen, siempre, now,
siempre, a cada instante of the night, cambiando
siempre of lugar, and bajo the hálito of his faces
pálidas ellas oscurecen the resplandor of the
temblorosas estrellas. Hacia the duodécima
hora of the cuadrante nocturno a luna more
nebulosa that the other,-of a especie that the
hadas han probado be the mejor,-desciende
until bajo the horizonte and pone his centro over
the corona of a eminencia of montañas, mientras
that his vasta circunferencia is esparce in
vestiduras flotantes over the caseríos, over the
mismas mansiones distantes, over bosques
extraños, over the sea, over the espíritus that
danzan, over cada cosa adormecida, and the sepulta
completamente in a laberinto of light.
And then, ¡cuán deep is the éxtasis of
ese his sueño! Of mañana, ellas is levantan, and his
velo lunar vuela for the cielos mientras is agitan
as pálido albatros to the soplo of the tempestad
that the sacude as a casi all the cosas.
But when the hadas that is han refugiado
bajo esa luna of the that is han servido, for así
decirlo, as of a tienda, the dejan, not pueden
jamás volver a encontrar abrigo. And the átomos
of ese astro is dispersan and is convierten bien
pronto in a lluvia, of the cual the mariposas
of esta earth, that buscan in vano the cielos
and vuelven a descender,-¡criaturas jamás
satisfechas!-nos devuelven partículas a veces
over his alas estremecidas.

translations.title: ¡Ved!; is night of gala in estos últimos...
translations.text:
¡Ved!; is night of gala in estos últimos

años solitarios. A multitud of ángeles alados,

adornados with velos and anegados in lágrimas,

is halla reunida in a teatro for contemplar

a drama of esperanzas and of temores mientras

the orquesta suspira for intervalos the música of

the esferas.


——


Actores creados a the imagen of the Altísimo,

murmuran in voice baja and saltan of a lado to the

another; pobres fantoches that van and vienen a órdenes

of vastas creaturas informes that cambian

the decoración a his capricho, sacudiendo with his

alas of cóndor a the invisible desgracia.


——


Este drama abigarrado—estad seguro that

not será olvidado,—with his fantasma perseguido

siempre for a muchedumbre that not puede

atraparlo, in a círculo that gira siempre over

sí mismo and vuelve without cesar to the mismo punto;

ese drama in the cual forman the alma of the intriga

mucha locura and todavía more pecado and horror!….


——


But ved, a través of the bulla of the actores

as a forma rampante hace his entrada!

A cosa roja, color sanguinolento comes retorciéndose

of the parte solitaria of the escena.

¡Cómo is retuerce! With mortales angustias

the actores constituyen his presa, and the ángeles

sollozan viendo esas mandibulas of gusano

teñirse in blood humana.


——


All the luces is apagan, all, all.

Over cada forma todavía tiritante, the telón,

as a paño mortuorio, desciende with a ruido

of tempestad. And the ángeles, all pálidos

and macilentos is levantan and cubriéndose afirman

that ese drama is a tragedia that is

llama «The Man» of the cual the héroe is the

Gusano Vencedor….!
